name: Bear Essentials: Account Manager
author: bearbrandingco

sections.description:
Sometimes the simplest things are surprisingly difficult to find.

We got tired of waiting for straightforward solutions to everyday WordPress
problems, so we decided to make our own.

Bear Essentials: Account Manager gives WordPress and WooCommerce customers a
simple way to permanently delete their own accounts, with password confirmation
and built-in safeguards. No fuss, no unnecessary complications.

Simple for customers. Sensible for administrators.

  • Easy account deletion: A self-service form on the account page, including
    WooCommerce My Account where available.
  • Password confirmation: Helps prevent accidental or unauthorised deletion.
  • Built-in safeguards: Checks relevant records and outstanding obligations
    before proceeding.
  • WooCommerce support: Handles supported order and privacy records carefully.
  • Supported integrations: Additional protections for specific plugins, such
    as Flintop Giveaways, where entries or prizes may require attention.
  • Request Help: Gives customers a way to contact the administrator when
    deletion cannot safely proceed.
  • Administrator control: An immediate ON/OFF switch, disabled by default,
    including after upgrades.

When an account passes the checks, the plugin processes deletion and confirms
the result. If a safeguard blocks deletion, it explains why and offers Request
Help instead. Administrators can review requests under Users > Account Deletion.

Part of Bear Essentials, a growing collection of straightforward WordPress
plugins from Bear Branding Co. Useful tools, thoughtfully made, without
making simple things unnecessarily complicated.

Security and data handling

Deletion requires the saved administrator toggle to be ON. Existing installs
are reset to OFF when upgraded, even if a legacy server switch was true.
BEAAM_ENABLE_SELF_SERVICE_DELETION=false in trusted site configuration always
overrides the toggle and prevents enabling it. The plugin never changes that
configuration. A legacy true value alone does not enable deletion. Staging and
production use the same guarded process; no allowlist or test helper is required.

Password confirmation, a user/session-bound nonce, POST-only processing, HTTPS
(except explicit local environments), throttling, per-user locking and repeated
safety checks protect the operation. Privileged roles and multisite are not
supported. The ordinary customer/subscriber must be signed in.

Completed WooCommerce orders do not automatically prevent deletion. Supported
WooCommerce privacy APIs and the site’s existing order-erasure choice determine
anonymisation or invoice preservation. Orders are detached, not deleted, and
financial totals/currency are verified. When invoice identity remains, standard
unnecessary contact/shipping/tracking and customer-note fields are minimised.
The site owner remains responsible for justifying retained information.

Outstanding/unknown orders, download rights, unresolved subscriptions and
customer-authored content can require help. Previously used integrations that
become unavailable fail safely rather than assuming their records disappeared.

WooCommerce and supported integration safeguards

Account Manager checks relevant customer records before allowing deletion. For
WooCommerce, this includes outstanding orders and other supported obligations.
It also supports specific integrations, such as Flintop Giveaways, where ticket,
winner or instant-win records can require administrator attention.

For Flintop, any detected historical ownership record causes a hold, including
closed or archived entries. A closed draw does not necessarily settle a prize
obligation. These checks can still apply when the integration is inactive.

When deletion is blocked, Request Help keeps the account intact and opens a
request for administrator review. It does not automatically settle obligations,
transfer entitlements or bypass safety checks. See the bundled documentation
for further technical limitations.

Privacy

This plugin has no telemetry, remote service, license server or customer-email
transport. It stores request status, timestamps, original numeric customer ID,
help messages/replies, processing receipts and pseudonymous signed audit events
in the site’s WordPress database. Existing administrator notes and approvals
are preserved. Passwords are checked with WordPress and are not stored by this
plugin. Necessary order records, request evidence and audit records may survive
account deletion and plugin uninstall; free-text messages may contain personal
information. Site owners must explain and justify retention in their privacy
policy and minimise unnecessary identifying text. WordPress privacy exporter
and eraser callbacks disclose retained request evidence; this is not a guarantee
that external services, independent app tokens or backups have been erased.

Audit identifiers and signatures use separate, randomly generated installation
keys stored in a non-autoloaded WordPress option. They do not use WordPress
authentication keys, cookies or salts and survive authentication-salt rotation.
Preserve these keys with your secured database backups. Missing or invalid keys
stop new signing/deletion rather than silently replacing keys for existing
evidence. Old salt-derived records remain unchanged and are labelled as legacy
signatures, not cryptographically verified. See AUDIT-SECURITY.md.

Compatibility and limitations

Version 1.2.6 separates audit and order-comparison cryptography from WordPress
authentication secrets. Existing interface and deletion protections are retained.
Password, identity, order, competition, audit and completion checks are unchanged.
Installed testing used WordPress 7.1.3, PHP 8.2, MySQL 8.4, WooCommerce 11.2.1
with HPOS and Flintop Giveaway 13.5.0. Standalone/absent-integration behaviour
passed isolated WordPress API contract tests. This is not a claim that every
WordPress/PHP version, theme or third-party extension has been tested.

Controlled staging tests verified empty-account deletion, deletion with a
preserved completed order, and protection of an unresolved prize. Later RC.2
tests verified status-independent ownership detection without deleting accounts.
The order-anonymisation branch has isolated contract coverage; equivalent
installed destructive testing was not repeated.

Successful completion is shown only after verified account removal and saved
completion evidence. WordPress sessions are revoked. Erasers are not one atomic
transaction: a later failure can leave some data erased and require recovery.
Do not blindly retry an incomplete operation.

Existing requests and signed audit evidence are preserved, including on
uninstall, and may contain personal data requiring the site’s normal review.
External processors, custom stores, separate app tokens and backup copies are
not universally erased. Mobile-app and public-page/store-declaration checks
belong to each site’s deployment, not a bundled app-store certification.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Upload Bear Essentials: Account Manager and activate it.
  3. Open the plugin settings and configure account deletion.

Using WooCommerce?

Customers can access account deletion through their My Account area.

Account deletion is disabled by default and must be enabled by an administrator.

For manual integration and advanced configuration, see the included
INSTALLATION.md documentation.
sections.changelog:
1.2.8

  • Simplify public installation instructions and direct advanced users to the
    included documentation.
  • Documentation and version metadata only; no functional changes.

1.2.7

  • Refresh the WordPress.org description and add four real interface screenshots.
  • Documentation and version metadata only; no deletion logic changes.

1.2.6

  • Replace authentication-salt-derived audit signatures and identifiers with
    independent installation keys; preserve and clearly identify legacy records.
  • Use request-local random keys for order-erasure comparisons.
  • Preserve default-OFF execution, identity checks and integration protections.

1.2.5

  • WordPress.org submission preparation: nonce sanitisation, native style loading,
    compatibility metadata and GPL license text. No new deletion functionality.

1.2.4

  • Add Return to Homepage after successful deletion using the native home URL.
  • Keep completed requests in View History, without deleting any evidence.
  • Hide replies for deleted accounts; preserve existing security and safety checks.

1.2.3

  • Add a clear empty-request message and My Account explanation; tidy admin spacing.
  • Presentation only. No functionality, security or deletion-behaviour changes.

1.2.2

  • Add an immediately saved, administrator-only ON/OFF toggle to Account Deletion.
  • Keep new/upgraded installations OFF; server-side OFF overrides take priority.
  • Update plugin description. No customer-deletion or integration workflow changes.

1.2.1

  • Remove the built-in staging account allowlist; use the same process on staging
    and production when explicitly enabled. Execution remains OFF by default.

1.2.0

  • Final distribution of tested 1.2.0-rc.2; version labels and documentation only.
  • Standalone WordPress support with optional WooCommerce and Flintop checks.
  • Status-independent stored ticket, winner and instant-win ownership protection.
  • Existing request, approval and audit compatibility; execution OFF by default.
